_doc: Q23's ratchet (threat model v2 M5/M6, Al Kowalski's coverage gate). Per source family and RHEL release, the residue this corpus is ACCEPTED to carry. Residue may SHRINK -- a better parser classifies more -- and may never GROW, and the `unparseable` subset may never exceed its cap. Same shape as content-src/flag_coverage_baseline.json and read the same way: the gate fails on a REGRESSION against these numbers, not on the numbers themselves.
_why_residue_is_the_metric: ADR-002. A coverage percentage invites the parser to classify more by classifying worse. Residue counts the lines this parser DECLINED, with a closed reason code for each, so the only way to move the number is to read a line correctly that was not read before. It is published, held and ratcheted rather than reported.
_pinned_by: Milo Vance corpus refresh, reconciled by Jordan Patel and Zee Carter under Benny's recovery authorization after current main added the RHEL 9 captures. The new raw_captures/RHEL 9 cell is now measured instead of accepted empty; pinning the fresh current-main run makes the next increase a failure.
_retire_note: A ratchet with no end date stops being a countdown and becomes the plan (MCR-SEC-020 condition F3). By the retire-by date the residue reason mix is re-read and the baseline re-pinned deliberately, or the gate fails and says who owns it.
_unrated_note: M6. A mined record is never `green` -- nobody reviewed it -- so nearly all of them are `unrated`, and that is correct. What must not happen is the fraction GROWING: that would mean the tier is getting LESS rated over time, the opposite of the direction it moves once records start being reviewed.
